hypotheses.justification:
The bound holds for every real C. Put a = |C| and choose a natural N > 2a. There exists D ≥ 2a such that, for every prime p, both |1+C/p| and |(1+C/p)⁻¹| are ≤ 1+D/p. The first inequality is immediate. For p > N, the second follows from |1+C/p| ≥ 1-a/p and (1-a/p)⁻¹ ≤ 1+2a/p; the finitely many primes p ≤ N can be absorbed by increasing D. Zero factors cause no problem because their inverses are zero.

Taking products gives |singularFactor C j| ≤ singularFactor D j and |(singularFactor C j)⁻¹| ≤ singularFactor D j. Using Real.abs_rpow_le_abs_rpow, Real.rpow_neg_eq_inv_rpow, Real.rpow_le_rpow and Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le, each summand is therefore bounded by singularFactor D j ^ ⌈|r|⌉₊. Apply singularFactor_nat_moment with the nonnegative parameter D. Its exponential constant is positive. These comparisons include zero bases (Real.zero_rpow and Real.rpow_zero), negative bases, and empty products; U = 0 gives an empty sum.
